content: what a brave person. i admire her courage in facing this situation. im 29 now and was diagnosed with leukemia three years ago. i was lucky that it was controllable with molecular targeted drugs. all i had to do was take pills every day and at one point i was even motivated/fit enough to do a triathlon. but nothing in this world goes smoothly. sadly, this treatment was too strenuous for my body and last summer i unexpectedly came down with pulmonary hypertension and heart failure triggered by it. i was hospitalized for 1 month and fully recovered now (i think). they took my off the drug for a few months (my body felt so "light" without having to consume those chemicals) but the tumor marker started coming back up and now i am on a different pill, which has less side effects but belongs to an older and slightly less effective generation. whats tough for me is that i initially had hope. i believed everything would be fine, that one day my life would go back to normal. but the reality that things may not go as planned started to sink in since the hospitalization incident and this has really bothered me the past months. the fact that my work life is competitive/stressful (i choose this job so shouldn't be complaining), that my current pills can be fatiguing at times, that i live alone and cannot discuss my worries with anyone including colleagues/friends (some people walk away when they find out about my condition, so i stopped talking about it with people), has also been picking away at my mental armor. i think the key is to make peace with what may potentially come and i can really tell that has helped pat improve her qol. maybe its time to truly face my emotions and maybe that will change the course of my life, however long that may be.

content: i normally love your videos but this one is flawed outright from the outset. first a correction on 13 and 7. chapter 13 is not a "luxury of the rich". often times 13 is actually a failed attempt at 7. there's a thing called a means test where the court forces a party to restructure in ch 13 if they have the means to pay off their debts. this prevents more capable applicants from simply walking away. that said, you were so close to being right when you talked about corporate structures. bankruptcy does not exist so people can rip off lenders by writing off their consumer debts. it exists to imcentivize risk taking. if you take out a loan to invest in an company or product, something absolutely needed for the economy to run, bankruptcy allows you a way to protect your personal assets. if bk didn't exist, only those with sufficient wealth to bootstrap a business would be able to capitalize on innovations and even they would be substantially more risk averse. yes, like anything it can be abused and yes, like anything the wealthier the party, the more they can benefit. however, it's an injustice that a guy who defaults on 20k in unsecured debt can simply bk out of it, not an injustice because he lacks the assets to need risk mitigation strategies.

video_title: Alcohol, Hangovers & How to Cure a Hangover Based on Science | Dr. Andrew Huberman
content: for those who get horrendous headaches after drinking try this. obviously a hangover is/can be a mixture of headache, tiredness, hanxiety and bad stomach. luckily i've never had a bad stomach from a hangover and all it makes me do is wanna eat more. i can mentally put up with any hanxiety and tiredness is not the end of the world. but i have always suffered from horrendous headaches when drinking. and i love a good drink. over the years i had just put up with the headaches as a sacrifice worth making for the enjoyment of a great night out. but a about a year ago i started questioning why i got such horrendous headaches from drinking when some of my pals seemed to get away with it. i went on line and researched headaches from drinking and everything said that it was from dehydration and losing essential salts and electrolytes from your system as your body urinates all the alcohol out as fast as possible as it sees it as a poison. the dehydrated causes your brain to swell and that's what causes the headaches. well how can i combat that i thought? these fizzy rehydration tablets seemed to suggest they were great at replacing all the salts and electrolytes. and for swelling anti inflammatory medication is what's usually took. so i gave it a go. and what i find is if i know i'm gonna be drinking a lot on say a saturday night, i take a hydration tablet when i get up in the morning. just before i go out i take a couple of ibuprofen tablets. i put some by my bed with a glass of water and some hydration tablets too. when i get in at silly o clock in the morning i neck a pint of water with another hydration tablet and two more ibuprofen. when i wake up in the morning if i've followed this regime i swear, the difference between that and not doing it is chalk and cheese. i go from feeling like death warmed up to just quite tired. i neck another pint of water with a fizzy hydration tablet and two ibuprofen when i wake up and that sees me through for the rest of the day. instead of a debilitating hangover which leaves me unable to do anything but sit still on the sofa watching tv, i can pretty much function as would normally if id say was feeling like i needed to catch up on some sleep. i even make it to the gym sometimes now too. it might not work for everyone but if headaches are crippling for you after a night out partying hard try it.

video_title: Man Shares End of Life Realities After Terminal Cancer Diagnosis
content: tanner martin, a 25-year-old diagnosed with stage 4 colon cancer in 2020, shares his journey alongside his wife, shay wright. initially, tanner experienced digestive issues and blood in his stool, which he and doctors attributed to benign causes. medication temporarily alleviated symptoms, but they returned severely six months later, accompanied by fatigue. a colonoscopy revealed a large tumor blocking his colon, leading to a stage 4 diagnosis with metastases to his liver. despite aggressive treatments—12 rounds of folfox chemotherapy, 20 rounds of folfiri, 50 rounds of radiation, multiple surgeries, and smaller procedures—the cancer was deemed incurable in 2023. tanner also battled sepsis from june 2023 to january 2024, requiring extensive hospitalization and halting cancer treatment. the ordeal caused significant weight loss (100 pounds) and physical decline. facing a terminal diagnosis with a 14% five-year survival rate, tanner and shay focus on living fully, traveling to italy and ireland, adopting a cancer support dog, visiting disney world, and meeting mark hamill through the dream foundation. they held a "living funeral" to celebrate tanner’s life, planned end-of-life details (e.g., $23,000 funeral costs), and share their story on social media to process grief and raise awareness. tanner, a therapist with a master’s in marriage and family therapy, emphasizes early screening, noting the rising incidence of colorectal cancer in young people (including 11-year-olds in his support group). he advocates for life insurance and proactive health checks, having inspired others to get colonoscopies that detected precancerous conditions. tanner’s legacy is to encourage preparation for worst-case scenarios and living life fully despite fear.

content: i'll be 80 in november 2025 80. !!! if my doctor told me that i was going to die, say, in 6 months, what about that news would make me feel like i was facing a great loss? why do we want to avoid dying? well, sometimes it's because we want to see our children or grandchildren grow. sometimes we have a life's work that we want to complete. sometimes we don't want to leave a loved one alone. but, basically, we fear dying because we don't want not to be. we don't know what it's like not to be anymore. we hold on to this world even when life isn't so great. we have cares and worries and concerns and fears . these weigh us down! will there be enough money? will i end up in some grim state run 'facility ' without being able to get to a toilet ?? will i live in pain? will i lose my ability to communicate my thoughts and needs and desires? will i lose my mind? will i end up on the street? will i be alone? given these possible prospects, the idea of avoiding them by dying would seem appealing. but as bad as life might get, it's all we have ever known. it feels like this world and our place in it is so real!...like it is the only reality. maybe we are wrong. but, what else is there except this world and our presence in it? what happens to the body when we die? it degenerates, dissolves ...it's constituent parts are disassembled . we go back to where we came from...the universe of atoms. we go back to eternity where time and space don't exist. suddenly, being a conscious, self aware living human seems a truly marvelous thing. a rare and precious opportunity ....to experience life ! maybe the earth and our life on earth is unique. then, why have we been so cavalier about our existence if it is so precious and special? why have we been so wasteful, so petty? so unloving, so selfish? so hurtful? what is going on here??? in my kitchen, recently, i have noticed these practically microscopic ants crawling across the counter. so small, i sometimes don't notice them until they move. i think, what does being alive mean to them? do they think, feel? normally, if some kind of bug gets into my place i make an effort to get it out. open the door or the window and shoo it away. i prefer not to kill it. but these ants are so minuscule that i don't hesitate to simply press my finger on them. they leave no trace. they disappear ! they were alive and suddenly, they don't exist! like turning off a light. the natural world looks upon us objectively. in the play, ''marat/sade'', de sade says that death is simply a part of a process and that "every death, even the cruelest death, drowns in the total indifference of nature". he believes that nature would remain impassive "if we destroyed the entire human race". does our existence have a purpose or is it just a meaningless part of an apathetic cosmos? what does religion say? genesis says that our belief in this physical world is what separates us from the eternal. the belief that we can ever be separate from 'god' is the original sin. perhaps original error would be better. genesis tells us that belief in, trust in the reality of this physical world is an illusion. and that death therefore is also an illusion. but this physical world seems so real...and death feels like the end of everything. but...is it? i always wondered what people meant when they talked about having faith...believing in god or jesus. what did that mean? i think it meant having faith that even at the moment of death we are still in the presence of god...the eternal. that we can never be separated from it. that is what is meant by eternal life. knowing that there is no death. it's a tough thing to ask a person to believe, given the hard reality of this world. that's why people gather together once a week to re-affirm the belief that we are always connected to god and to gain strength from communal agreement. all this is theory. but i prefer it to living a selfish, greedy, uncaring,unloving and hurtful existence. trump and all his followers stumbling about in the dark causing pain. but maybe even trump is a natural phenomenon that we must accept just as we accept other natural disasters. just as the little ant must accept its instantaneous, unexplainable end. everything changes. things come and go. species, oceans, mountains . they all mutate . stars burn out. the earth brings forth infinite forms of life. they arrive, then they move on and are replaced. everything drops back into the immense design of things. why do we, as individuals and as a species, resist?

video_title: Luxury = Avoiding Poor People
content: this entire video is such a red herring so let’s break it down: - public transit is often dirty, poorly maintained, and unreliable. we aren’t living in tokyo where the train arrives at 8:17:00 and a delay of 60 or more seconds results in fines. often, relying on public transit means that a person is sacrificing an incredible amount of time just…waiting. also, i don’t know about you, but i generally prefer that my morning commute not be permeated with the fragrance of eau d’urine. - high-cost neighborhoods are often quieter, better maintained, more visually appealing, and — mostly importantly — have better funded school districts. ignoring your third point for a moment, if an individual wanted their child to have access to the best possible public school education, they almost *have* to live in a high-cost housing area. that aside, though, you typically won’t find high-income communities that are riddled with trash and litter, have people coming and going at all hours of the night, or generally have disturbances. given that almost all of the residents of such neighborhoods are working professionals with 9-5 jobs, they not only tend to be quieter, but also seem to maintain their space better, since they had to work so hard to achieve it. - sending a child to private versus public school has little to do with classism and a whole lot to do with the quality of education that child will receive. we’re living in an era where americans’ functional literacy rates are the lowest they’ve been in decades. the standards for standardized tests have had to be lowered because so many students nation-wide are at risk of failing. i don’t want my child to be in an educational environment where the expectation is that (s)he will barely scrape by — i want him/her to be in an environment where (s)he will be challenged to succeed, where the students have more access to 1:1 learning and mentorship from teachers, and where the school isn’t struggling to fund basic programs. i can’t get that at the vast majority of public schools. - summer camp is a boon to working parents. children who aren’t old enough to stay home by themselves need to be looked after, and parents who don’t have the luxury to stop working for three months are often left with the choice of either (1) babysitters or (2) summer camp. between these two, summer camp is actually the more economical option. again, this has little to do with classism and almost everything to do with the practical necessity of needing to work while your child is off school. the fact is that most people who acquire disposable income aren’t trying to get away from “poor people,” they’re trying to get away from people and environments that are messy, dirty, loud, rude, ignorant, and inconsiderate. not *all* low-income communities are that way. not *all* high-income communities are spared those characterizations. but if you try to deny the reality of that trend, you’re living in willful ignorance.

content: just the truth a child could understand. brian is a grown man on the outside, but his inside is still like a scared little boy. he wants love, but he’s afraid of it. he likes closeness, but when closeness asks him to show up, he hides. he enjoys attention, but responsibility makes him freeze. he wants to look strong, but he feels weak when someone needs real emotional things from him. he cares about people, but he doesn’t know how to take care of their hearts. imagine a turtle: when things feel easy, the turtle comes out of his shell. when things feel big or serious, he pulls his whole body inside and pretends he’s not there. that’s brian. he doesn’t disappear because he hates you. he disappears because feelings overwhelm him and he never learned how to stay present when things matter. you didn’t do anything wrong. he just doesn’t have the tools. he can be kind. he can be gentle. he can be fun. he can make someone feel special in small ways. but those things aren’t the same as being able to stay when someone needs him. a five-year-old can give hugs and be sweet, but a five-year-old cannot be a partner, cannot be stable, cannot hold someone’s emotions. that’s the gap. he doesn’t know how to talk about hard things. he gets scared of being wrong. he gets scared of disappointing people. he gets scared when someone he cares about gets upset or vulnerable. and instead of saying: “i’m scared,” or “i don’t know what to do,” he runs away or shuts down. not because he doesn’t care. because he doesn’t know how to be a grown-up when emotions show up. when one person is afraid to carry feelings, the other person has to carry everything. it makes you feel like you have to tiptoe, hold everything together, keep things calm, make sure nothing upsets him. that’s why you walked on eggshells. you weren’t crazy. you were compensating. brian is not a bad man. brian is not a strong man. brian is not an evil man. brian is not a grown man in the ways that matter. he is a little boy in a big body. a little boy who wanted love but didn’t know how to receive it or return it. and when love became real, he got scared and hid inside his shell and never came back out. that’s the whole story.

content: as a result from a very severe tractor trailer accident (blew out a steer tire and went over an embankment into a bunch of trees) i was entrapped in my cab for over 1 1/2 hours. during this time i coded twice. thankfully i had some wonderful paramedics and first responders. i coded a third time in transport to the trauma center once again being resuscitated. what i can tell you from these occurrences are that what comes after us being here is that what awaits us is much more beautiful. it is free from pain, free from the noises and smells and fears and anxieties of life. you feel you are in a warm place that feels so welcoming, a place that wants you to be there and is glad you came. you get a feeling all over your body of an immense childhood like excitement… the coming down the steps on christmas morning or perhaps seeing that old friend or family member you haven’t seen in a very long time. (i just got goosebumps thinking of this again). please, if this is you and you are going through this, please know that what you have ahead of you is beautiful. the pain you will feel and the fears you will face will only be temporary and will be well worth it. you will always be with your loved ones in blood and heart and with their memories. (when i coded i could actually “see” my children and what they were doing. i don’t think they saw me, but i had the feeling that i could still be with them. of course i don’t know if that is permanent or my chance to say a final goodbye.) we will all die one day, our bodies will be laid to its final rest, but our spirits and souls will live forever and you will once again be with all your loved ones.

video_title: Why is it so hard to escape poverty? - Ann-Helén Bay
content: why is it so hard to escape poverty? this video does something important. it dismantles the myth that poverty is simply about motivation or effort. instead, it explains the poverty trap, how benefit cliffs, unstable wages, rising costs, and rigid eligibility rules actually punish progress. people can lose healthcare, childcare, food assistance, or housing supports the moment they earn slightly more, even when that income is still not enough to survive. so, working harder can literally make life worse. the animation makes it simple, but the message is heavy; systems built without flexibility create cycles that are incredibly hard to escape. what struck me most-especially reading the comments is how many people share the same lived experience: afraid to accept a raise losing benefits overnight choosing between medical care and rent working full time and still going hungry that's not individual failure, that structural design. the video also highlights what does help: gradual befit phase-outs, access to childcare, healthcare continuity, education, transportation, and policies that support upward mobility instead of penalizing it. this reinforces why we don't just help people cope - we advocate to change the systems themselves. poverty isn't a character flaw. it is a policy outcome. powerful, compassionate. and absolutely worth watching.

throw them away, but he had purposely placed them someplace. i did a quick scan, are they still within reach? no. the next day at lunch i decided it would be a good time to feed my dad's ego, ask him to keep me company, and i'd bring up how i couldn't find the dog's things so he could inform me and look good, feel like he'd solved the problem for me. when i asked him he stared at me like i was crazy and said "i don't remember where i put them." i forgot that when you deal with a narcissist they have made a plan. this was a multi-step thing for him. i had stepped into the first trap. now i was supposed to get mad and react and freak out because my dog's things had "gone missing". i instead told him he was lying, that no one misplaces something as important as a living animal's things. he got very mad about this and insisted he'd go right then and look. he came back perfectly happy, as though he had never been mad and told me "they're on the wire shelves by the boxes." i told him, "the entire garage is lined in wire shelves full of boxes. which ones?" i made him pinpoint it down. when i went out to look for myself later, the basket had suddenly appeared in a perfect line of sight from the door, this to make me question if i'd somehow not seen them. my dog has 2 neon giant rubber balls. no, i would have seen it. no, i did not overlook his items the night before. my dad was playing a game with me. it's hard to explain to people that he never factored in the fact that he was not only doing this to me, a living person, he had involved another living thing in the mix. people might say, "well the dog and you weren't in any danger here." actually, that's exactly the point that people don't understand. it's always there in my mind, not "if" but "when" he might take it to another level. a lot of my time is spent trying to keep things at the level they are so nothing on his end escalates to that point. but i know he's not happy that the game didn't work that time, so straight. there's no way to explain how the more you visibly fight to the narcissist the worse it will get. he needs to think things are status quo. he needs to think that i'm in worse state than i am day better than the last, and deal with the drama he tries to stir up with as little a reaction as possible so he gets bored of me and moves on. anyway... posting this here in case it helps explain what the hell this kind of stuff looks like, or helps others feel less crazy. it's not us. it's them, trying to make it look like its us. always.

content: escaping poverty and achieving a more secure and prosperous life is a journey that involves a combination of practical steps, mindset shifts, and perseverance. here are some practical methods and ways to help you on this path: 1. education and skill development: formal education: completing high school or pursuing higher education can significantly increase your earning potential. vocational training: acquiring practical skills through vocational schools or apprenticeships in trades like plumbing, welding, or as an electrician can lead to well-paying jobs. online courses: numerous online platforms offer free or affordable courses to learn new skills in areas like coding, digital marketing, or graphic design. 2. financial management: budgeting: create a detailed budget to track your income and expenses. this will help you identify areas where you can save money. saving: even small amounts saved regularly can grow over time. aim to build an emergency fund to cover unexpected expenses. debt management: if you have debt, create a plan to pay it off as quickly as possible. high-interest debt can be a major obstacle to financial security. 3. increase your income: negotiate a raise: if you are employed, research your market value and negotiate a higher salary. side hustle: consider starting a small business or finding part-time work to supplement your income. seek better opportunities: don't be afraid to look for a new job that offers better pay and benefits. 4. build a support system: mentorship: find a mentor who has achieved the financial success you aspire to. they can provide guidance and support. networking: connect with people in your field or community. networking can lead to new opportunities. community resources: many non-profit organizations and government programs offer assistance with housing, food, and job training. 5. cultivate a growth mindset: believe in yourself: a positive mindset is crucial. believe that you have the ability to improve your financial situation. set clear goals: define what financial security means to you and set specific, measurable, achievable, relevant, and time-bound (smart) goals. stay persistent: the path to financial security can be long and challenging. there will be setbacks, but it's important to stay persistent and never give up on your goals. however, by taking these practical steps, you can significantly improve your chances of breaking the cycle of poverty and building a more secure and prosperous future for yourself.
